claims.text: Incorporating WS2 into a ceramic matrix composite will enable self-lubrication over a wide temperature range.
The lamellar structure of WS2 facilitates low-friction sliding.
Adding WS2 will maintain the mechanical strength of the ceramic matrix composite.
The introduced WS2 particles will retain a lamellar microstructure within the ceramic matrix.
The WS2-reinforced composite is intended to operate from room temperature to approximately 1000°C.
The layered structure of WS2 permits easy shear along its basal planes.
WS2 forms a self-lubricating layer during sliding.
The WS2-derived lubricating layer reduces friction.
The ceramic composite matrix sustains the load-bearing capacity while WS2 provides lubrication.
WS2 reinforcement will significantly reduce the friction coefficient relative to the unreinforced composite across the tested temperature range.
WS2 reinforcement will significantly reduce the wear rate relative to the unreinforced composite across the tested temperature range.
The WS2-reinforced composite will retain its mechanical strength or experience only a modest strength reduction relative to the unreinforced composite.
Agglomeration of WS2 particles may limit the predicted tribological benefit.
Degradation of the ceramic matrix beyond the tested temperature range may limit the predicted benefit.
